sources.entry: Padlock - A minimal, open source password manager for macOS.

summary.one_liner: Padloc is an open-source password and data manager for individuals and teams, organized as a monorepo of server, web, desktop, mobile, and browser-extension packages.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Padloc as simple, secure password and data management for individuals and teams. The repo is split into packages: core logic, a web UI component library, a backend server, a Progressive Web App client, localization/translations, an Electron desktop app, a Cordova project for iOS and Android, a Tauri native app, and a browser extension. To run it locally, the README gives steps to clone the repo, install dependencies with npm workspaces, and run `npm start` to serve the web client. A `npm run dev` mode starts the server (default port 3000) and the PWA together. The README also covers Prettier formatting, unit tests, and Cypress end-to-end tests. Hosting a production instance and building distributable apps are said to be covered by guides "coming soon." The README does not mention macOS specifically.
use_cases: run a local password vault for testing
build a custom password manager client
develop a browser extension or desktop password app
notable: Monorepo with separate packages for server, PWA, desktop, mobile, extension, and shared core logic
Runs locally with a single npm start command
Includes a security whitepaper describing its design
Licensed under AGPL with a commercial license option
caveats: Production hosting and app-build guides are described as coming soon
Dependency footprint is kept deliberately small, and contributors are asked to justify new dependencies
Commercial use outside AGPL terms requires contacting the maintainers for a commercial license
